tasks.title: Bar chart: recycling in five countries
tasks.prompt:
The chart below shows the percentage of household waste that was recycled in five countries in 2000 and 2020.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

visual.title: Household waste recycled, 2000 and 2020
visual.note: Fictional data created for practice purposes.

examinerNotes: Overview should note: recycling increased in all five countries; Dunmark had the highest rate in 2020 and the biggest increase; Corvia had the lowest rate in both years; Estova led in 2000 but grew least.
tasks.modelAnswer:
The bar chart compares the proportion of household waste that was recycled in five countries in 2000 and 2020.

Overall, recycling rates rose in all five countries over the twenty-year period, but the size of the increase varied greatly. Dunmark went from the middle of the group to the top, while Corvia had the lowest rate in both years.

In 2000, Estova recycled the largest share of its household waste, at 40%, followed closely by Belmora at 35%. Dunmark recycled 22%, whereas Arland and Corvia recycled only 12% and 8% respectively.

By 2020, the picture had changed considerably. Dunmark's recycling rate had risen by 36 percentage points to 58%, the highest figure on the chart. Arland also made remarkable progress, with its rate almost quadrupling to 45%. Belmora's figure increased to 52%, putting it in second place, while Estova, which had been the leader in 2000, saw the smallest rise, reaching 47%. Corvia remained far behind the other countries: although its recycling rate almost doubled, only 15% of its household waste was recycled in 2020.

tasks.title: Causes and solutions essay: fewer young farmers
tasks.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, fewer and fewer young people are choosing to become farmers.

Why is this happening? What can be done to encourage more young people to work in farming?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
tasks.modelAnswer:
In many parts of the world, the average age of farmers is rising, because few young people are willing to take over farms or start their own. This trend could threaten food production in the future. This essay will consider the reasons for it and suggest some possible solutions.

The main reason is that farming is often seen as hard work with low and unpredictable income. Farmers work long hours in all weather, and a single drought, flood or fall in prices can wipe out a year's earnings. Many young people therefore prefer jobs in cities, where salaries are more reliable and working hours are fixed. A second reason is the cost of starting a farm: land and machinery are extremely expensive, so it is almost impossible for young people without family land to begin farming. Finally, rural areas often lack good schools, healthcare, entertainment and fast internet, which makes them less attractive places to live.

Several steps could make farming more attractive. Governments could offer grants and low-interest loans to help young people buy land and equipment, and insurance schemes could protect farmers against losses caused by bad weather. Agricultural colleges could promote modern farming, which uses technology such as drones, sensors and data analysis, to show that farming can be a skilled and innovative career. Investment in rural infrastructure, especially internet access and transport, would also allow young farmers to sell their products online and enjoy a better quality of life.

In conclusion, young people are turning away from farming because of low and uncertain income, high start-up costs and limited rural services. Financial support, a modern image of agriculture and better rural infrastructure could help reverse this trend.
